correctness.rationale: The claim is proved for the exact domain \(m=15/16\) and \(0\le\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*\). The support measure remains nonnegative; at \(\varepsilon_*\) the only zero of one curvature radius occurs at the active-arc endpoints, so interior active support faces remain singleton and the reducedness proof still closes by endpoint limits. The source area expression is exactly quadratic in \(\varepsilon\). Exact rational interval bounds certify \(C_2<0\) and \(A'(\varepsilon_*)>0\), which proves strict monotonicity over the entire continuum interval rather than by sampling. The same certificate proves the stated area interval and comparison with \(\pi/4\).

value.rationale: The lead paper explicitly reopens a reverse-isominwidth extremal problem and invites optimization of its family. Solving the canonical fixed-m slice exactly is mathematically motivated: it identifies the active curvature constraint as the optimizer, proves the source parameter is not optimal even within that slice, and improves the explicit area lower bound by about 0.000968. This is a complete natural one-parameter classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice or mere recomputation.
